summary.short: Colombian Law 1273 of 2009 adds Title VII BIS to the Penal Code, criminalising computer-related offences against information systems and personal data, plus a computer-means aggravating circumstance; it applies to any person and takes effect on promulgation.
summary.long: Law 1273 of 2009 inserts Title VII BIS, 'Protection of information and data', into the Colombian Penal Code (Art. 1). Articles 269A-269H criminalise unauthorised access to computer systems, obstruction of systems or telecommunications networks, interception of computer data without judicial order, data damage, use of malicious software, violation of personal data, and website or DNS spoofing to capture personal data. Articles 269I-269J criminalise computer-assisted theft and non-consented transfer of assets, and penalise making or possessing programs for these offences. Article 269H raises penalties by half to three-quarters for aggravating circumstances, including attacks on state or financial-sector networks, conduct by public servants, and disclosure or gain. Article 2 adds use of computer, electronic or telematic means as an aggravating circumstance to Penal Code Art. 58; Article 3 assigns these offences to municipal criminal judges. The law applies from promulgation and repeals contrary provisions, notably Art. 195 of the Penal Code. Prison terms and fines in minimum monthly legal wages are stated for each offence.

notes: The text is a publisher compilation (Avance Jurídico, updated 30 Sep 2026) of the 2009 enacting law. Publisher markers appear without their content: '<Ver Notas del Editor>' in art. 269A and a 'Notas del Editor' heading before art. 269B. The text gives no bill number, legislative history or enabling clause, so no enacted_by_bill or legal_basis rows are recorded. The repeal in art. 4 is general, with one named article. Target instrument IDs are empty because the Código Penal and Código de Procedimiento Penal are not in the registry.

definitions.note: The Act has no definitions article. Scope-relevant terms such as 'sistema informático', 'datos informáticos', 'datos personales', 'software malicioso' and 'medidas de seguridad informáticas' are used without a definition in the text.

obligations.note: The operative provisions (arts. 269A-269J, plus the amendments to arts. 58 of the Penal Code and 37 of the Criminal Procedure Code) define criminal offences, aggravating circumstances, penalties and a court-competence allocation. Per the codebook these are enforcement or infringement lists, not obligations. Art. 4 sets the entry-into-force rule. No positive duty on a named addressee, and no duty on a public body, is stated.
